sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 18739 of 2024

Petitioner :- Mohammad Atif
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Ashish Pandey

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of petitioner in the Court today is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. for the respondents.

3. The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 10.7.2024 registered as Case Crime No. 261 of 2024, under sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C., P.S. Jawan, District-Aligarh.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While filing the supplementary affidavit learned counsel for the petitioner states that the petitioner is having criminal history of seven cases, which has been duly explained but learned A.G.A. has objected the same and on the basis of instructions submits that the petitioner is a habitual offender and he is having a long criminal history of nineteen cases.
5.
Considering the allegations so leveled in the First Information Report, we do not find any good ground to entertain the writ petition.

6. Needless to say that initially there was no discloser of criminal history but through supplementary affidavit the petitioner has tried to make up his case for quashing the F.I.R.
7.We have perused the FIR, which prima facie discloses cognizable offences against the petitioner and therefore, the prayer made to quash the FIR cannot be entertained in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017)
2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others reported in (2021) SCC Online SC 315 and as such, we are of the view that no interference is warranted.
8.

sentences.text:
However, considering the fact that all the offences, complained of, in the impugned FIR, are punishable with a term upto seven years, therefore, in case of effecting the arrest of the petitioner in pursuance of the impugned FIR, it is directed that the respondents/ authorities shall ensure that the specific provisions contained in Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of Cr.PC/Section 35 (3) to 35 (7)
of Bhartiya Nagrika Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as the directions issued in judgement and order dated 28.01.2021 of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 17732 of 2020 (Vimal Kumar and 3 Others Vs. State of U.P. and 3 Others) reported in 2021 (2)
ACR 1147, be strictly complied with.
9.
